pr_title: Fix SystemIOWindows handling of relative paths
pr_body:
The handling of relative paths in SystemIOWindows was broken by changes for #4256.

Change SystemIOWindows.PrefixWithUNC to only prefix paths with `\\?\` when they can be prefixed; i.e., only prefix paths that are fully qualified and that don't contain relative path components like `.` or `..`.  This way, relative paths passed to SystemIOWindows methods work correctly again.  Also support network paths specified using forward slashes; e.g., `//example.com/share/foo.txt`.

Simplify SystemIOWindows.GetFullPath since Path.GetFullPath will honor `\\?\` prefixes and can replace forward slashes with backslashes, etc.

Copy and adapt source for Path.IsPathFullyQualified from https://github.com/dotnet/runtime, which is MIT licensed.

Add unit test for Duplicati.CommandLine.BackendTool to validate the fix.

This fixes #4632.

issue_context.title: Duplicati.Commandline.Backendtool Problem with GET file:// in Version 2.0.6.3_beta_2021-06-17
issue_context.body:
- [x] I have searched open and closed issues for duplicates.
- [x] I have searched the [forum](https://forum.duplicati.com) for related topics.

----------------------------------------

## Environment info
- **Duplicati version**: 2.0.6.3
- **Operating system**: Windows 10
- **Backend**: file

## Description
A GET with the commandline to a file: Backend does not work with 2.0.6.3. If I execute the same command with my previous version 2.0.5.1 (on same PC to get the same file) the command is successfull.

Compare [https://forum.duplicati.com/t/duplicati-commandline-backendtool-problem-get-file-after-update-to-2-0-6-3-beta-2021-06-17/13264/2](Duplicati Forum) where the user ts678 confirmed the behaviour on an other windows pc.

## Steps to reproduce
1. `Duplicati.CommandLine.BackendTool.exe GET "file://\\hulk\backup_rw\duplicati\local-03_hulk_data" duplicati-b4d2dfe9739124b1292308bcf3e0016d4.dblock.zip.aes`
2. Works with 2.0.5.1 => file is downloaed
3. Switch to 2.0.6.3 and execute again

- **Actual result**:
`Command failed: Die Datei "\\?\duplicati-b4d2dfe9739124b1292308bcf3e0016d4.dblock.zip.aes" konnte nicht gefunden werden.
System.IO.FileNotFoundException: Die Datei "\\?\duplicati-b4d2dfe9739124b1292308bcf3e0016d4.dblock.zip.aes" konnte nicht gefunden werden.
Dateiname: "\\?\duplicati-b4d2dfe9739124b1292308bcf3e0016d4.dblock.zip.aes"
   bei System.IO.__Error.WinIOError(Int32 errorCode, String maybeFullPath)
   bei System.IO.File.InternalCopy(String sourceFileName, String destFileName, Boolean overwrite, Boolean checkHost)
   bei Duplicati.CommandLine.BackendTool.Program.RealMain(String[] _args)
`
[Englisch: The file ... could not be found. Filename: "\\?\..."]

- **Expected result**:
Should download the file!

## Screenshots
Command output pasted above.

## Debug log
If someone responds how to change the command line to get this output I will add the debug output here.
comments: I can't reproduce on Linux.  This could be related to the changes from pull request #4256.  @dferreyra, are you able to reproduce this?

@warwickmm, yes, I've just tried it now and get the error with 2.0.6.3:
```
Duplicati.CommandLine.BackendTool.exe GET file://\\... duplicati-20190010T10000Z.dlist.zip.aes

Command failed: Could not find file '\\?\duplicati-20190010T10000Z.dlist.zip.aes'.
System.IO.FileNotFoundException: Could not find file '\\?\duplicati-20190010T10000Z.dlist.zip.aes'.
File name: '\\?\duplicati-20190010T10000Z.dlist.zip.aes'
   at System.IO.__Error.WinIOError(Int32 errorCode, String maybeFullPath)
   at System.IO.File.InternalCopy(String sourceFileName, String destFileName, Boolean overwrite, Boolean checkHost)
   at Duplicati.Library.Common.IO.SystemIOWindows.FileCopy(String source, String target, Boolean overwrite) in Duplicati\Library\Common\IO\SystemIOWindows.cs:line 405
   at Duplicati.Library.Backend.File.Get(String remotename, String filename) in Duplicati\Library\Backend\File\FileBackend.cs:line 230
   at Duplicati.CommandLine.BackendTool.Program.RealMain(String[] _args) in Duplicati\CommandLine\BackendTool\Program.cs:line 137
```

The relative file name that's being passed in, "duplicati-20190010T10000Z.dlist.zip.aes" in my case, is getting the UNC prefix applied, turning it into the file shown in the exception.  I don't think that `\\?\` prefix works with relative file names.

If I instead provide a non-relative path, the command works; e.g.:
```
Duplicati.CommandLine.BackendTool.exe GET file://\\... C:\Downloads\duplicati-20190010T10000Z.dlist.zip.aes
```
This can be used as a workaround.

I'm thinking the answer is that relative paths need to be turned into non-relative paths via, say, `PathGetFullPath()`, before being passed to `FileCopy()`, etc., and maybe that's what was done in some places in the original commits, but I'll need to remind myself of the changes in those original commits before I can be sure.
Sorry it's taken so long to get to this.  I have a fix I'd like to propose.  I'll submit a pull request later today so folks can look at it.

I've submitted a pull request with my proposed fix.

Like I say in the commit message, the changes I made in #4256 made it so that many methods in SystemIOWindows would no longer work with relative paths (or with absolute paths with relative components like "..").  Specifically, the `\\?\` was prepended to many paths passed in to SystemIOWindows methods, but that can only work when the path is absolute and needs no additional "parsing" from Windows.

My proposed fix changes the code so that `\\?\` is prepended only when it appears safe to do so.  This way, if relative paths are passed in, they get passed on to the basic .NET methods unchanged and behave like they're supposed to.

This bug has been in place for a while now, so it seems like relative paths aren't encountered too often in Duplicati.  Still, before I had a good picture of what was going on, I did look to see if I could find all the places where relative paths could make it through to SystemIOWindows, and I found dozens of places that would need investigating if a fix were to be applied at those sites instead of fixing SystemIOWindows itself -- mostly in Duplicati.CommandLine.* programs.  Restoring relative path handling in SystemIOWindows made the most sense to me, especially since I think anyone looking at the code would expect SystemIOWindows methods (and by extension, ISystemIO methods) to work with relative paths.
Thanks @dferreyra!  Yes, fixing the code that adds the `\\?\` seems like the right approach.

@dferreyra Sorry I am not a aware of the code. But you write sometimes in your analyse about "relative paths". Just to clearify: My fiven file-Backend path is not relative! It is an absolute path: file://\\hulk\backup_rw\duplicati\local-03_hulk_data

Hi @Domalar, you're right about the "file://..." part, but the second parameter, "duplicati-b4d2dfe9739124b1292308bcf3e0016d4.dblock.zip.aes" is relative in the sense that the BackendTool is supposed to place "duplicati-b4d2dfe9739124b1292308bcf3e0016d4.dblock.zip.aes" in the current directory for you.  The bug I introduced with #4256 makes it so that that Duplicati can't create that file.  If, instead, you use an absolute path for that second parameter; e.g., "C:\temp\duplicati-b4d2dfe9739124b1292308bcf3e0016d4.dblock.zip.aes", the BackendTool would then be able to create the file, even with this bug in place.
